Dim Forest Ecological Survey (1)

The environment of the Confinement Woods is even more magical than expected. A unique canopy ecosystem has formed around the branches of this giant tree.
According to my investigation, the tree's branches contain abundant Resonance Energy within. The energy gathered from around the area of the Dim Forest travels from the top of the tree to the entire trunk. Under the catalyst of this energy, such a huge tree was formed. And it is by relying on these energies that the tree reproduces a whole different ecosystem. Probably because of the ferocious roars that come from time to time within the tree, the tree has no signs of activity from large MO or TD. This gives the plants a better chance to flourish and allows the Remnant Mutterfly to exist.
The skills of the Resonator who created this giant tree is very similar to mine. I guess he is also a nature lover. Otherwise, even with the assistance of the sonic instrument at the top of the tree, it is unlikely that such a large and complex giant tree could have been created.
In order to facilitate future expeditions, I made a little fluorescent decoration on the branch of Confinement Woods as a sign. This will make future research expeditions more efficient. So it's time to go, to explore the depths of the Confinement Woods!

Battle Log No. 6010: Battle for Point 91.7

11 nights witnessed the battle for the 91.7 highland. Our XXX lost 16 men, including our deputy. 7 serious injuries and 8 mild injuries. The battle progressed as follows:
In late November, the enemy assaulted our 9.17 highland, which was not named. For days of nights of fighting and contending, most of the surface of the highland was occupied by the enemy. On October 27, we received the command to go in to battle and back up friendly forces.
Under fire cover, our force launched 6 strikes on the enemy with 8 hours, all of which failed to drived the enemy away from the highland.
Early 28 morning, the enemy launched an unresultful counter-strike with covers of cannon firing.
From Octboer 28 until Nov 6, the control ot the highland was transferred back and forth a few times, but there weren't decisive results for both sides.
Night Nov 6, my force was replaced by a friendly one which would take on our duties due to the severe headcount loss of more than 70%.
Summary of Battle:
The loss of my force was predominantly done by close-range fire. This, for one, proves the defense insights about indirect fire circulated within the army; for another, it makes the case for the underpreparation of my force with respect to close-range crossfire. Detailed battle review is attached hereafter.
Battle Log No. 6010: Reorganize

It is November 8 today. We retreated to our rear for rearmament as per the order. The rumbling of cannons keeps coming through from 91.7. No doubt that highland is to be the key to the whole battle. The side that takes it takes control.
On that highland, which hardly covers some ground, flesh and blood have become the strongest defense lines. All the steels knee before them.
I am glad I didn't borrow the deputy's new clothes, for at least he can be taken home with pride.
He told me a tale, which he said was told by his grandfather, that when one passes, his homecoming soul will be hitched with breezes to where he belongs. Now it's late night, I wonder if my comrades are on their way to return.
Battle Log No. 6010: Departure again

On Nov 15, we met the backup we waited for: two recruits. Together with the 12 men left, we formed a squad. Since we kept the establishment of XXX, my title of acting deputy squad leader was nominally acting deputy XXX leader.\nThe battle at 91.7 drained our reserves. It's time the undermanned forces, that is us, be sent back to the front. We are infiltrating into enemies' rear. As soon as the encircle is done, we will be positioned to annihilate the enemy.\nThe enemy has realized this. They are planning a desperate sally intended to break our front and encircle our flanks in turn. The fate of this decisive battle is soon to be seen.

...
It took me a long, long time to learn how to speak again. Even longer to find the courage to open this diary.
The woman who saved me from those monsters called herself a professor from Startorch Academy. She's beautiful, but she doesn't look like anyone from our village. She told me I have a rare kind of Forte, something that makes me a "potential Synchronist."
I told her everything that happened to the village. I asked her: is this a blessing from <ano=the Exostrider>Baldur</ano>? Or the cruelest curse <ano=the Threnodian>Hvedrungr</ano> ever devised?

She crossed an ocean so vast I can't even imagine it, all to find a way to free the world from this fate. She asked me to join the Academy. She said that whether my power is a blessing or a curse, it might be the key to opening the door to our future.
...But I have nothing left. Even if <ano=the Exostrider>Baldur</ano> is waiting behind that door, it can't give back what I've already lost.
...
I went back to Granny's place to say goodbye and thank her for everything. I told her I was leaving for the Academy.
"We Roya carve our words into stone," she said, her voice as kind as ever, "so that <ano=the Threnodian>Hvedrungr</ano> cannot erase our existence. And those children at the Academy use something they call 'Cassettes' to do the same. To me, you're just going somewhere else... to carve the statue that belongs to you."
"As long as the memory remains, so does the soul."
After I arrived at the Academy, I read this notebook from the very first page to the last. Papa, Mama, Fenrir, Dallas, Bori... Granny was right. They're still alive here in these pages, and deep within my mind. Maybe, without even realizing it, I've become a living statue carved with all their names.

...

I've spent my life trying to outrun its shadow. It's one of <ano=the Threnodian>Hvedrungr's</ano> venomous tendrils, dragging everything I love into the nothingness. I thought... I thought I had learned how to ignore it.

Just like the professor said, only I, only my Forte, can save that village from being wiped out. I couldn't save my own home back then. But this time, I won't stand by and watch the dark take the people I love.
It's time to go.

It's been forty-eight hours. I don't think they'll find us now.
 
You've done well, old friend. This is where your journey ends. I never expected a Sabercat Reaver. Without the proper tools, I can't fix you.
 
It seems I was born worthless and will die the same. I had originally hoped for you to record the effects of the Void Storm on the human body and the surrounding environment when I entered it, then deliver the data to the Spacetrek Collective. A coward's last shred of dignity.
 
The Academy will find the note in my room soon enough. Yes, this is a journey to die. I intend to let the Void Storm take my life.
 
Perhaps someone will find this journal long after I'm gone. Let it serve as my farewell to you, stranger.
 
Forgive me for leaving without a proper farewell. Please understand, this isn't a sudden impulse, but the final compromise after a long and painful struggle.
 
As a researcher who once held science as my faith, I believed that the pursuit of knowledge is civilization's most noble mission. My field once granted me glimpses of the universe's profound beauty. Those elegant equations on the blackboard seemed to guide me toward pushing open the doors of progress.

But perhaps every era is destined to face the same tragedy. Researchers believe they stand on the shoulders of giants, only to look down one day and find themselves standing on the ruins of their own idealism. Failure, after failure, after failure... Was this always my limit?
 
That's when a colleague reached out. He claimed he could help me overcome my technical bottlenecks, but everything had to be done in secret. I later discovered he was a Fractsidus spy. On the day he was captured, he never revealed our collaboration. He only left me with a smile. What was he smiling at? That I was next? Or that I was no longer the man I used to be? In our work together, I had already crossed lines that violate scientific ethics.
 
The purity of knowledge in my eyes had long been corrupted. Whenever I heard my colleagues' praise during academic conferences, I felt my stomach twist. Their admiration was evidence of my betrayal of science.
 
Death is all that's left for me now. But even though my soul is sullied, I wish to leave one last, small thing of value before I go.
 
The Void Storm. None would volunteer to enter it. I imagine if someone would go into it... It would certainly garner data of immense value.
 
I do not seek forgiveness, nor do I expect to be understood. I only hope my departure becomes a question mark, lingering in the minds of those who still believe in the purity of knowledge...

Death only gives one chance. I can't waste it. First, I must observe the Void Storm. Perhaps I'll stay with the Roya tribe until I'm ready.

Time has lost all meaning to me. It's nothing but a countdown now.
 
I haven't encountered the Void Storm yet, but I've learned much from the Royan archives. Their records speak of survivors. What allows one to live through it? Where is the line that decides what gets erased and what remains?
 
Ugh... this fever won't break. I should set aside these heavy thoughts for today.
 
Why is it that whenever I relax, I am reminded of the Roya tribe members from when I first arrived?

I watched them live alongside the Exoswarm, toiling with simple tools. I saw them observe the night sky and strange phenomena with their own eyes, patiently calculating, step by step, summarizing patterns.
 
At night, they would sit around the campfire. No one dwelled on the day's troubles. They simply planned for tomorrow, then sang a song with a strange, simple, repetitive melody, as if speaking to Lahai-Roi. Or perhaps it was their way of encouraging themselves.

Watching the firelight dance on their faces—wrinkled and young—a profound confusion struck me.
 
We, in our "advanced" civilization, seek to master nature through technology, to eliminate all uncertainty and pain. When progress stalls, we despair, even betray our morals for a breakthrough. We believe human dignity lies in "conquest."
 
But for the Roya... even though a "small" storm could wipe away everything they worked so hard to build, they show no despair. Their dignity isn't about "conquest." Instead, they chose silence. Time and time again, they bend their bodies, measure the broken land with their feet, and begin anew.
 
I once despised this "inefficient" struggle, seeing it as a sign of an unprogressive society. But now, what rises in my heart is… respect.
 
Such a feeling of contradiction claws at me from the inside. The "pure science" I've pursued my entire life, if it ultimately led me to betrayal and nihilism, then where is its purity? These tribal people, who knew nothing of "science" at first, have proven a more fundamental purity through their very existence—the will to struggle and live, no matter how many times they're beaten down.
 
Here I am, the lofty professor, brought down from my high horse. I'm driven to suicide by the "impurity" of my ideals, while they, with their hands in the dirt, fight to live. In that struggle, they embody life's truest purity.
 
The rain outside grows louder, much like their song… I'll leave once the fever breaks. I need to get closer to the Void Storm, to understand it more. My old droid friend may be broken, but I still have a way to record it all. If I remember correctly, there should be an Outcast camp up ahead.

This is likely my final recording. I haven't formally introduced myself yet. I am Sestan, a professor from Startorch Academy.
 
I don't know what awaits me now...
 
I was perched at a high point, recording data on the Void Storm. While adjusting my instruments, I saw a mech reindeer, unaware, drifting too close to the edge of the distortion. Slowly. So slowly. I knew an invisible force would snuff out its fragile life in an instant.

In that moment, my mind went blank.
 
I did not weigh the value of life, did not calculate the odds of success, did not look back on a lifetime of sins and confusion. My body acted before any rational thought could intervene.
 
I rushed forward and pushed the reindeer out. And I was pulled in instead.
 
Life is full of surprises. To be honest... I had already let go of any thought of suicide. This journey, the people I've met along the way... they showed me how.
 
In the Roya tribe, I witnessed the strength of the human spirit. In the Outcast camp, among fellow traitors, I learned about forgiveness from their struggle to survive. Everyone was just trying to live, while I was wallowing in self-pity, clinging to the guise of an idealist.
 
My life and my ideals had strayed from their path. And so... in this moment, I rushed forward. Not just toward death, but toward a reunion with the true spirit of science: to protect life, no matter how small.
 
Before I vanish completely, I'll try to remain conscious. I will record my physical sensations and the frequency fluctuations, then upload the data to this Cassette and a data drive. Consider this my final observation report. I hope it proves useful.
 
Body temperature: normal... Wrist movement: normal... Feet, hmm... losing sensation...
 
………………
 
Twenty-three minutes have passed...
 
…………
 
Hmm... Death, is it always this quiet? I used to think my students were too noisy. But now, haha, I find myself missing the noise...
 
External sound... decaying rapidly...
 
Hmm... after the sounds disappear, will the light go next...?
 
Finally... I'm home...

As the Express through the Rain II

Unsullied by doubt, you nod. In your full skirt, the rain is returning to the skies.
The express, descending from the air, carries you away with strong whistles.
Then, silent neon lights are smashed to the ground and feed me the splashes.

Then, I get swallowed by that rainy night.

As the Express through the Rain III
All our dreams disappear in the heavy rain, as they evaporate in the aching land.
The spreading fire burns every vein and valve, so as the rain drops about to meet the ground.
I see crawling petals come out of the soil, tearing down the foundation with their bodies. I can only escape, stumbling through the night and howling rains as I cling to the past shadow of you.

If my mail could finally reach its shores, perhaps I'd earn myself the title of a valuable courier! I'm sure that I'll find the chance! Hehe!
Because our topic here is: Lo, Lo, Lollo Logistics! I want to be a proud courier today! Hmm, I nearly forgot... Address... What's the address for our next order...

Lo, Lo, Lollo Logistics! Part Two
Lo, Lo, Lollo Logistics! I want to be a proud courier today!
Now that I've mentioned sounds, maybe the friction when the breeze gently laps on our uniform deserves to be on the list! I could hear the roaring gales as I ride the express car to deliver my orders. It serves as a reminder during my journey, urging me to hurry my pace with louder chants.
But please note that safety is the first on the road! Because you may bump into dangerous Tacet Discords that look pretty alike to traffic lights. Just follow the rules: red for stop and green for go, keep this in mind every time! Or you'll catch the attention of vicious monsters! No one can predict the situation around the port, since Tacet Discords are haunting us with their looming existence... It even gets worse when we have to commute between here and the obsolete port... 
Oh, that used to be a place of glamour like Port Gunchao, according to Miss Lumi. But the transportation was ruined by the sudden appearance of the fault zone. To make things worse, Tacet Discords started to pop up from nowhere... Later, the port could only bid farewell to its busy days and sink into dust. Such a waste. I think many packages are held up in the port to this day... Well, that's not what you expect of an express. I wonder if these packages could finally meet the right ends...
Maybe our new supply station will do the trick? Okay, my next workplace is settled then! Lo, Lo, Lollo Logistics! I want to be a proud courier today!

Lo, Lo, Lollo Logistics! Part Three
Lo, Lo, Lollo Logistics! I want to be a proud courier today!
Continuing our topic on the sound... I don't think I can skip the strange murmurs from Whining Aix's Mire. No, those are totally INSANE!
Let me explain in detail: I've made a transfer request to the new supply station. But some Exiles lurking in the neighbors just raided our camp and robbed us blind. I can't believe this... I know these aren't just common packages, they're potent representations of feelings. Miss Lumi agrees with me. On our first encounter, I already knew her as an impressive navigator. Though young, she deals with every order with delicacy, and that allows her to locate the fastest route despite all the obstacles and rubble along the way. When she delivers a package, intact as it is, to her customers, she ends her service with a radiant smile. How sweet...
By the way, Exiles are just one subtle part of our difficulties. Take the dense fog in Whining Aix's Mire for example. It usually signifies an accompanying thunderstorm and shrill screams that bring up a ripple of sadness and... a sense of longing. That's where the navigation tends to fail as the fog gradually consumes you.
Devastating events. I can't quite picture myself overwhelmed by such dense fog and Siren sounds... Eek! I can't dwell on this. Time to get back to work and be a proud courier today!
Lo, Lo, Lollo Logistics!

Untitled Family Letters II
I found this letter after Xiaobao went to bed.
Don't worry... Everything is fine now. Xiaobao helped me a lot. Though strange things happened under the mine, that's no sweat at all to my job. We take care of ourselves, and you should too.
You reminded me of my father, a soldier who seldom came home. I missed him so much and kept asking my mother the same question: When would he come back? But the war was escalating and those Tacet Discords were approaching our doorsteps. I remember a courier delivered a mail on a rainy day. I could tell right away that it was from my father. I came out of my room with a happy smile, when the courier paused for a conversation with my mother. Turning around, she cried over my shoulder, shedding tears upon that letter I dared not to read it myself.
I know they sacrifice a lot to drive those Tacet Discords out of Desorock Highland... and you're now suffering in bitterness at the front line. That gentle knock on the gate still chants a scary echo for me to linger upon the slightest thought that you would die like my father. So I told the couriers to leave those letters on my doorstep.

Untitled Family Letters III
Worry not, dear. I'm doing fine these days. We managed to defeat a small group of Tacet Discords, while the Ministry of Development is working on some large-scale defense projects. Untitled Family Letters IV
...I don't know how to start this letter. General Jiyan, I want to say thank you. Thanks to you, his message finally reached us like this.
I recall days with him from time to time. He said someone should be the protector, even if this means sacrifices. In those distant portrayals of the battlefield, you stood unwaveringly against the enemies, supporting him and other soldiers with your might. He said you saved his life countless times. You are his icon, the best soldier who possesses a fighter's heart and a giver's will. He wants to be the same. Although he'd sacrificed his life to cover his teammates, I don't think he'd ever regretted it.
That's what you told me, that he always protects other soldiers even when facing the greatest threats, that he deserves to be a hero.
That night, I met him in a heart-breaking rainy dream that ominously resembled the day when the death of my father arrived. He opened the door, greeting me with his comeback. The early reunion obliged me to ask him: Why did you come back? I thought the war was still raging.
He replied: I just want to check if you're safe. Xiaobao is asleep, right? I'll be leaving now if everything is okay.
And then he added: Everyone on the battlefield just can't mellow out one bit when the war is drawing to an end. They're prepared to go for the killing blow.
I nodded: Just do your job and don't worry about us. Be a fearless fighter and beat those monsters. His steps paused upon a hesitant yes. I urged him to go back, and in anxiety, I met his open arms. He asked me: What if I die in the battle? What about you and Lil. Bao?
Questioned by such a dilemma, I asked in return: Do you ever regret joining the army?
He said no, not if he can protect our homeland.
"So am I." I said.
When I woke from that dream, I was visited by a sudden idea to see the Hero Play with Xiaobao. In the Theater, the heroine in Fiamma wielded a sword bravely against the Fluffernox while the stage bathed in flames. Attacked by the monster, she fell to the ground again and again. As she gathered herself from continued sufferings, tears coursed through my face. I told Lil. Bao that his father is a hero who can rival the Fiamma.
Xiaobao answered this in excitement: I want to be a hero just like him!
I promised to share all these stories with him and all living souls.
General, I would remember this till the end of life, and carve those names upon an eternal stone.

I received a message the other day.
Nothing special, just a message from the train station to the delayed passengers. It reads: "The Future Express apologizes to you with utmost sincerity. We'll keep our service full and complete until you reach the destination." I finished reading and deleted it, thinking "This must be a mistake by the station. I haven't traveled by train for a long time."
But this was just the beginning. I kept receiving strange messages about this Future Express now and then. I transferred them to the spam at first. I live in the moment. Those sorts of long travel and future seem out of my realm. I'm busy running errands around the mine, listening to frequent complaints from those researchers. Even a small miner like me gets a little bit nervous as the year draws to its close.
But these constant messages are killing me. Once I snatched a moment from my job to check them up and one particular piece had captured my attention (probably from a kid): "Daddy. The steward tells me to sit tight because the train is about to leave. We'll be in the future in no time! She would cast a spell that keeps us safe until the train arrives at the future. But I don't know about the future..." These words reminded me of my daughter, the same ever-curiosity when she was young. I haven't seen her in a while, though. I didn't want to disappoint this young sender with all the delay and wait. So I replied: I know the future. Future is where you get to eat Star Flakes and realize all of your dreams.
Several days later, this message thing struck my terminal again with a delay notice: "We're sincerely sorry for the delay. The Future Express will seek for soon departure while ensuring you a safe and happy journey with our best." It even ends with something like "The Future Express will meet you in the future." Another text comes right in: "When do we get to leave? Lil. You keeps asking me about this. I can only respond with empty promises, telling her that 'Soon we will be leaving for the future.' The lobby is full of anxious passengers, each clutching to an urgent desire to leave. And myself included. I received some food from a good Samaritan and that relaxed my nerves a bit. *sigh* When do we get to leave..." This looks like a message for the train station to me but somehow it reached my terminal. Glad that I had a soft time those days. Urged by a passing thought to cheer the sender, I replied: The train will leave soon. Be patient.
It never really cuts off the messages. I still receive them now and then. During a meal with my colleagues, I brought up the topic and all those intricate and haywire messages in my terminal. I sometimes felt compelled to comfort those frustrated passengers.
They said in utter doubt, that there was no such thing as the Future Express.
So I showed those messages to them and met their confused stares. The elder one of my colleagues chimed in, recalling some sort of rail station around the place in the past. It was used as an escape route during a horrible disaster. People named this train "The Future Express", carrying a message that you could ride with it until the bitter end and arrive at the future. Ages had veiled the rest of the story when they only came along the tongues of the past generations. Even he didn't know what happened later. I can't help but think, if the Future Express truly belongs to a forgotten past, then why would I receive these messages...
Strange Messages

Title: Spectrum Anomaly Monitoring Report for Subject C-001

Entry: #H-C-6947

Abstract:

The data presented in this report were obtained from spectrum evaluations performed on Subject C-001, also known as "Jué," from June ████ to December ████.

During a preliminary experiment conducted on June 14th, ████ researchers observed a 15-second frequency loss in Subject C-001's spectrum. Five additional tests were later conducted through the following day, and all data obtained reflecting the frequency loss were highly consistent (Margin of error averaged below 0.02).

The recorded data of the Resonance Spectrum on the 3rd, 6th, 11th, 23rd, and 30th of the subsequent month indicated a gradual lengthening of Subject C-001's frequency loss. The data exhibited significant increases with varying patterns. It was postulated that this event occurred due to the presence of Subject C-002, also known as the "Mianloong Chamber." Subsequent thirty-two one-factor experiments confirmed a significant correlation between Subject C-002 and the duration of frequency loss in Subject C-001. Notably, Subject C-002 exhibited an inhibitory effect on the duration growth of Subject C-001.

Based on spectrum monitoring data of Subject C-001 from June ████ to December ████, the following preliminary conclusions can be drawn:

1. Subject C-001 bears defect/malfunction.
2. Subject C-002 can temporarily slow down the escalation of Subject C-001's defect, but cannot make up for Subject C-001's frequency loss.

Appendix-1 (Source: Research Memo #C349)

With the help of the "peculiar visitor", we were given the opportunity to converse with Subject C-001 directly. It was a meaningful and mutual conversation, though we didn't get as much information as I had hoped for.

But at the very least, the conversation proved one point: Our previous research was effective, and there was no defect in C-001. As per C-001's own declaration, "One of the Temporal Programs was lost," and during its prime, C-001 had the capability to manipulate time by decelerating or even halting it, rewinding it, and making corrections as needed. Nonetheless, the current condition of C-001 can be described as one of sickness, with irreversible disruptions to time rendering any attempts at correction or restoration ineffective. Consequently, Mt. Firmament has been transformed into an isolated entity amidst the vast oceans of time, despite the initial purpose being one of redemption.

Appendix-2 (Source: Research Memo #C382)

By running through time flow models, we came up with two hypotheses:

Hypothesis #1: C-001's "defect" is none congenital, and this "defect" may have taken place around the period of C-001's first arrival at Mt. Firmament (it has been confirmed that the "defect" cannot be reversed, see report #H-C-7426).

Hypothesis #2: The discrepancy in temporal progression between the interior and exterior of the "time bubble" has been progressively widening. Based on data comparisons, there exists a correlation between the deceleration rate of time flow in Mt. Firmament and the growth rate of the duration of C-001's frequency loss.

Expanding on the second hypothesis... If C-001 were to eventually cease to exist, the uncontrolled flow of time in Mt. Firmament would likely surpass its limitations and impact a broader range of regions… Such as, the entirety of Jinzhou.

…This might be why that "peculiar visitor" offered to work with us in the first place…

Appendix-3 (Source: Research Memo #C457)

Efforts are being made to advance the development of the artificial Resonance Object. Although we have not yet achieved success, we have decided to name it the "Chronosorter" in honor of our recent progress.

I know we have our "peculiar visitor" to thank for every progress we've made so far. If the "Chronosorter" project is successful, it's a win-win for everyone involved. As I had anticipated, they intend to restore and utilize C-001's complete power in order to rectify the temporal distortion, with the aid of a Resonance Object.

There is still a significant journey ahead of us. This is merely the starting point.

Excerpts from The Hammer of Heresy (The pamphlet presents several radical opinions that appear to reflect the theories of an extreme school of thought.) What is witchcraft? And what is its true nature? The power of Resonance wielded by Resonators is known as a blessing from Sentinel Imperator. Devout followers of the Order are granted this blessing by adhering to its precepts, allowing them to channel the divine force through mortal bodies. Witchcraft, however, arises from vain desires—faithless souls, drawn by Leviathan, form a contract to practice forbidden arts. In doing so, they forsake the divine blessing bestowed upon them at birth and abandon their humanity, transforming into witches who seek to taint the mortal realm with profane power. The Divinity has shaped our world, and all that we hold dear flows from Their blessings. Yet witches, seduced by the Arch Enemy, pervert these divine creations into impure, disgraceful entities, crafting a false Resonance with them. The enemy's mark upon these witches is proof of their transgressions. With the aid of the Vessel of the Enemy, they can even transform into Tacet Discords, posing a grave threat to Imperator's faithful followers. Caution is essential, for anyone who craves freedom and worldly desires is vulnerable to becoming pawns of Leviathan. Thus, we must regularly cleanse and exorcise such souls. If we allow these heretics to grow unchecked, wielding their tainted power to defile the mortal realm, they will inevitably bring the Dark Tide upon Rinascita. It is the Order's duty to guide and govern them, ensuring they align with Imperator's divine will. Should they refuse to join the Order, swear loyalty to Imperator's statute, or diligently uphold its teachings, their misguided fate will be set right by the Pilgrim's Sails. We shall pray for them day and night, that they may be saved by our Sentinel Imperator. Praise be to Imperator. The Spy Network of the Order the Deep Ah, my friend, my companion on this quest for freedom and truth, I implore you—open this pamphlet only in a secure place, away from prying eyes. What I am about to reveal is crucial to your safety. Learn now how to identify the spies of the Order the Deep and evade their grasp. All Echoes bearing a golden halo upon their heads are spies of the Order the Deep, serving as "Angels." They are always seen alongside the Acolytes, serving as the Order's minions to take out the heretics. Rinascita, the Land of Echoes? Ha... not even the greatest satire could ever truly capture the utter absurdity of the reality we endure. First, you must beware of those lantern Echoes, known as Lucerna. Though they may appear harmless, they possess the ability to reveal so-called heretics hiding in the shadows of the night. Their light can illuminate the path ahead, yet it also serves as a blinding weapon, causing one to lose their sense of direction. There was once an instance where someone used Fae Ignis's Echo ability to remain concealed, only to be exposed under the unforgiving glow of a Lucerna's light. Next, there are the most commonly seen plaster statues, the infamous La Guardia, the most loyal guardians of the Order. Without commands from the Acolytes, they stand motionless, like silent statues. However, if you find yourself pursued by La Guardia, do not waste time fighting them. Instead, focus on locating the Acolyte of the Order Penitentiary who is issuing the command. Among all these minions, the most detestable is Vox Sanctus, perched high atop the church buildings. They serve as the Order's guards of honor. While they cannot move freely, they use their instruments to preach false doctrines day and night. These sermons infiltrate the souls of the Ragunnesi, poisoning their thoughts. Can you imagine that the children of Ragunna are forced to hear this nonsensical preaching the moment they are born into this world? Oppression by force may still leave room for resistance, but in Ragunna, how can one escape the spiritual chains that seep into every corner of life? Laurel and Sword (Part I) Laurel and Sword: On the Divine Imagery in The Golden Bough Journal Title: Ragunna Sea Breeze Drama Society Research Journal, Volume 1 Category: Literary Studies, Literary Theory, Theater, The Golden Bough The Golden Bough, a Ragunnesi narrative epic rich in history and deeply influenced by primitive religious culture, is renowned for its prominent theatrical elements. The epic begins with pastoral plays that draw on the primitive beliefs and customs of various tribes during the Age of a Thousand Islands. As the story unfolds, these diverse narratives converge under the guidance of Sentinel Imperator. The author employs the perspectives of the Divine Envoys to provide Imperator's view, allowing the characters to assume their roles in classical plays. Throughout the work, recurring symbols of religion and totems appear, echoing metaphors commonly found in traditional plays. The use of these theatrical elements has helped establish the epic as a beloved classic, cherished by both officials and commoners in Ragunna. Furthermore, it embeds the author's profound reflections on the will behind the Oracle delivered by Sentinel Imperator, as well as the social changes occurring in the region of Rinascita. ...(Some of the pages are missing) One of the most commendable scenes in The Golden Bough is the concluding Scene 3, where five storylines dramatically converge at the climax of the Carnevale: the Holy Forest of the Fagaceae Peninsula, the Order of Ragunna, the Keepers of Secrets in Thessaleo Fells, the successor of the governor in Septimont, and the gladiators, all merging in a grand finale. In this scene, the author masterfully interweaves characters and plotlines, capturing the unique allure of a grand historical tragicomedy. This convergence in Scene 3 has served as a template, inspiring countless plays thereafter. The scene's influence owes much to its intricate plot design, which displays a skillful technique that sets a standard in narrative structure. Beyond the theoretical framework of the work itself, this design—where each element reflects the core theme and draws from historical settings—has solidified this epic as a timeless classic, maintaining its relevance and reverence across cultural shifts in literary history. (See Note 23) The Golden Bough is recognized as the earliest work of art to connect tribal folklore with the Sentinel (see Note 24). In the climactic Scene 3 of the Carnevale, the five masks stand together, each pursuing their own faith, when Sentinel Imperator descends from above, bestowing the laurel upon the chosen Enlightened One—the main protagonist on stage. This ritual has since become a lasting cultural emblem in the hearts of the people of Rinascita. From this scene onward, every heroic journey must conclude with the ritual of "being laureated," whether the hero takes on the role of an actor on stage or a playwright behind the scenes during the Carnevale. Laurel and Sword (Part II) Laurel and Sword: On the Divine Imagery in The Golden Bough Journal Title: Ragunna Sea Breeze Drama Society Research Journal Category: Literary Studies, Literary Theory, Theater, The Golden Bough (Continued) The reason for Sentinel Imperator's descent at the climax of the Carnevale in The Golden Bough remains an open question, one largely unexamined in the epic itself or in related research. Historically, the prevailing view in the Seminary held that the Laureate must be the individual who most aligns with Rinascita's ideals and resonates with the Sentinel—not driven by dramatic passion or ulterior motives. For a long time, this perspective dominated studies of The Golden Bough and the broader field of Laureate literature, with the laurel seen as a symbol of immense honor and the embodiment of Rinascita's collective will. (See Note 25) However, following the cultural events after the Seminary incident, the Laureate's symbol and performances are now seen as expressions of the Sentinel's divine will—the guiding force behind delivering the Oracle and unifying the doctrines. The image of laurel has also come to represent this sacred intent. The author raises an intriguing question: given this interpretation, could the selection of the Laureate itself be seen as an indoctrination of freedom—a concept seemingly at odds with The Golden Bough? Mom, I miss you.
It's pretty misty here, and whenever it's like this, I can't help but think back to when I was little, back when we were together.
We used to live in a house out in the countryside. It was a thatched cottage, and in the summer, I could hear the dried hay on the roof crackling as the sun beat down. In the winter, the walls would get damp.
Inside, the house had a narrow hallway that led to the kitchen, where a broken lightbulb, somehow always mysteriously fixed, hung from the ceiling. The exposed wires were wrapped in black tape.
Along the hallway were two rooms. I slept in the smaller one, the one on the north side. The gauzy curtains, printed with the sacred verses of the Order, always felt a little eerie at night. When I couldn't sleep, I'd sneak out to the narrow hallway. It didn't matter if I kept my eyes open or closed. With my back against the damp walls, it was pitch black, and I couldn't even see my own breath.
The wind tried to sneak in through the cracks, and the door frame seemed to shrink. The old wires were starting to tear, and the damp air pressed against the bricks. My hair brushed against the wall, and behind it, a patch of quilt slowly shifted. All these sounds tangled together in my head, floating from my ears to my skin, then rushing back inside, shaking my bones with a soft, mesmerizing tremor.
I can't shake this feeling of dampness that echoes in my mind. Today, it's here again.
I just passed through the misty barrier on our route. It felt like an unsettling dream.
But don't worry about me. The safety manual says this mist can cause hallucinations, but it's harmless. I've made it through safely. Now, I need to check the inventory again, just in case someone took something while I was dreaming.
I really miss you, Mom. Don't forget what I promised. Once I've made my name here, I'll bring you to Ragunna.

The Magistrate's menacing gaze pierced through the trembling woman like a hot knife through butter. "Sign this here contract and you'll belong to me, my dear. And as long as you don't break any of the rules for the next three years, I'll make your ex-husband beg for mercy and pray for a swift death."

The woman crumbled to the ground in tears, her once glamorous face now stained with mascara. She clutched onto the papers like they were her last chance at redemption. In an ironic twist of fate, her former nemesis had become her savior. Her hair was no longer the envy of onlookers, but rather hung lifelessly around her face like a wilted flower. "Fine," she choked out, "but I have one condition."

The Magistrate leaned back with a smug smirk on his face. "Go on," he purred.

"That woman? She needs to disappear from this world," the woman demanded, a glint of revenge flashing in her eyes.

The Magistrate's brow furrowed in confusion as he watched her tears. "Sure, " he said quickly, lifting her up with one hand and causing her to stumble into his arms. As she struggled against him, the Magistrate's expression softened and a hint of amusement danced in his eyes.

"Don't touch me!"

"Ha! Don't flatter yourself, sweetie," the Magistrate chuckled. "I wouldn't touch you with a ten-foot pole."

The Dim Forest is unquestionably the most significant treasure trove in the entire Huanglong region, boasting unparalleled species richness in the world.
Upon setting foot at the entrance of this gate, I could distinctly hear the plants whispering and their summons.
It is said that deep within the forest, the former site of the Department of Ecoacoustics holds image records of numerous plants, including a delectable species known as Ivory Banana, originating from the Dim Forest. Ivory Bananas were once a primary food source for Hoochiefs, and, in return, Hoochiefs exploring the forest in search of Ivory Bananas became excellent pollinators.
Since the spread of the toxic spore mist, wild Ivory Bananas have disappeared from the Dim Forest, and information about this species can now only be found in historical records.
The Lament might be an inevitable process of natural selection.
Dim Forest Ecological Survey 1

Guided by the fluorescent plants, I discovered a large purple tree.
Considering its characteristic of resembling an entire forest on its own, I speculated that this tree is likely a sub-species of the Ficus genus. The mysterious purple color on its leaves remains unexplained and requires further research and verification.
Due to the season, I failed to collect samples of the flowers and fruits of this tree, and there were no traces of pollinating insects in the vicinity. Surprisingly, the Violuna Banyan hasn't been contaminated by the toxic spores. Many mysteries still surround it, waiting to be unveiled.
I am certain that this is the first time this tree species has been discovered, and I have temporarily named it the Violuna Banyan.
Dim Forest Ecological Survey 2

After bidding farewell to the Violuna Banyan, I proceeded towards the most important target—the Central Banyan.
It's a tree towering into the sky, with a large spore cloud perched at the top, spreading toxic spores with the wind.
Any creature approaching this tree exhibited obvious anxiety and fear—the white toxic spores floated around the Central Banyan, almost blocking out my sight. I could even hear faint coughing from the forest. I needed to take every step with extreme caution from now on.
The closer I got to the Central Banyan, the more uneasy I felt—there was a heavy snorting coming from its hollow, and the vibrations caused by breathing shook off the spores accumulated on the branches. As more and more spores fell down, I tightened my filter.
These creations of the Waveworn Phenomenon are infiltrating our world, making everything dangerous and unfamiliar.
Dim Forest Ecological Survey 3

It's been a while since I had such an intense workout.

The contaminated Hoochief exhibited an astonishing lack of fatigue in their relentless pursuit of its prey—unfortunately, that prey was me. However, when escaping, I didn't feel panic and my brain started racing. I was well aware that the toxic spores are a direct consequence of the Waveworm Phenomenon. Based on the Ecoacoustics standards, how should we classify those contaminated Hoochiefs? Furthermore, how do those toxic spores contaminate Tacet Discords and is meditation a viable solution for Tacet Discords contamination?

Utilizing the Grapple function, I skillfully swung onto a hidden branch. The contaminated Hoochief lost track of its target and scanned around in confusion. It looked like a lost kid, whimpering and coughing, and it seemed to lose spatial perception. Each intense cough released a burst of toxic spores into the air. The spores, driven by their innate instinct to propagate, further pushed the already weakend body of the Hoochief to its utmost limit.

I started wondering: is it a form of co-evolution, or does it represent a parasitic relationship?
Dim Forest Ecological Survey 4

The social behavior of Hoochiefs is even more astonishing than imagined, establishing them as the dominant species in the Dim Forest.

According to my survey, the toxic spore mist constantly spreads outward from the Central Banyan. To avoid the invasion of those spores, Hoochiefs disperse into different groups, seeking refuge in various safe zones, gradually forming communities characterized by "paternalism". The intelligence displayed by those Hoochiefs seem to be unique among Tacet Discords. Besides, near the Hoochief communities, sightings of activities from other Tacet Discords are notably scarce, which I attribute to a possible manifestation of "territorial consciousness". This consciousness prompts Hoochiefs to take different jobs and collaborate in repelling intruders from their territories.

What makes me even more curious is the response of a community if a Hoochief becomes contaminated. I am left wondering about the decisions such communities would make in such a scenario. Along the frequented path of the Feilian Beringal, I caught a glimpse of some grave-like mounds. Unfortunately, I didn't have the time to examine them carefully.

The battle for 91.7 Heights lasted 11 days and nights, and our platoon, including the platoon leader and platoon deputy, lost 16 men, 7 were seriously wounded, and 8 were lightly wounded. The battle was as follows:
In late October, the enemy attacked my 91.7 unnamed heights, after several days and nights of repeated struggle, the enemy has encroached on most of the surface positions. 27 October, my department was ordered to put into battle to support friendly neighboring forces.
Under cover of fire, our unit launched six attacks on the enemy within eight hours, all of which failed to accomplish the task of expelling the enemy from the heights completely.
At dawn on the 28th, the enemy unsuccessfully launched a counter-attack with fire support.
From October 28 to November 6, control of the surface position changed hands several times, and neither side made a breakthrough.
On the night of the 6th, our department was replaced by friendly neighboring forces and withdrawn from the battlefield for repairs due to large losses and more than 70% casualties.
Lesson Learned:
The casualties of our section came mainly from kills by enemy close-range direct fire. This came to prove that the defensive experience promoted in the Army concerning indirect fire was effective; on the other hand, it proved that we were ill-prepared for close-range fighting, a detailed summary of the lessons learned is attached.
Battlefield Record 6010: 91.7 Highland Contest

Today is November 8, and we have been ordered back to the rear to reorganize. The rumbling of artillery at 91.7 is constantly heard, and there is no doubt that height will be the key to the whole battlefield. Whoever mastered it there gained the initiative.
Flesh and blood became the strongest line of defense on that high ground, which was not many square feet, and before which all steel had to bend the knee.
I was glad I didn't borrow the platoon sergeant's new clothes, at least we could bring him home with dignity.
He told me a legend that his grandfather told him. It is said that when a man leaves, in the dead of night his returning spirit will be carried back by the breeze to find his own home. Now that it's late at night, I wonder if everyone has already set off on their way home?
Battlefield Record 6010: Reorganization

Since we were still a platoon, I was the acting squad lieutenant, nominally an acting platoon lieutenant.\nThe battle of 91.7 had depleted the reserves, and it was time for us to return to the battlefield with the remnants of our incomplete formation. Our troops are penetrating to the enemy's rear, just waiting to complete the encirclement so we can completely annihilate the enemy.\nThe enemy has also realized this and intends to make a desperate attempt to break through our defenses and counter-encircle our two flanks. The fate of this battle will soon be decided.

The person who escapes from the lacquered black abyss need not deliver any warnings.
 
It seemed to mock us as it danced within the swirling whirlpool. The blue crystals on its back gleamed, barely a few centimeters above the dark, rushing waters. The harpoons we had sunk into its back were gone, but we did leave three glaring holes behind!
 
Every time we neared it, it swam faster into deeper waters. The deeper it sank into the whirlpool, the faster it swam, but for us, there was no turning back.
 
It vanished first, and when it reappeared beside our port, one mast was already submerged, and the other snapped off.

I lay on the beach, alone. There was no ship, no crew, and no sign of it.
 
I had none of its blood on my hands, no ship's wheel, no ropes, no harpoons. Nothing to grasp onto. 

But the sea breeze felt unfamiliar. I realized I'd never set foot on this beach before. Since we set sail from Cape Bedford, I remembered every passing port and beach, but this one... this one was unfamiliar.

Yes, in time, I found Starbuck and Queequeg on this island. They're still alive. "It," the whale they call "Cetus the Tidebreaker," was also still alive.
 
How can this be a "blessing"? This is nothing but a "curse!" I cannot accept this!
 
Once I've had my vengeance, death may take me. But if my vengeance fails, I cannot bear to remain in this world as a mere plaything for those I sought vengeance against! My fate is mine to decide, and only true death can end my conquest.
 
They don't understand. That whale, though it appears tame and gentle, is cunning and violent. It transforms death into an unjust eternity, making my vengeance just a footnote in its mockery of the sea… No, I will never accept this. I will never compromise!
A Sealed Confession: Part 2

All whales carry oil, and this oil can dissolve many things that water cannot. This is the conclusion we reached after crossing every sea.
 
It can dissolve things of every shape and nature into one, and there are even stories of people who fell into a whale's oil-filled brain and drowned, with no bones ever found. But I have never seen what oil this whale holds... Perhaps I never will.
 
More than twenty years have passed, and Pequod seems cursed. No matter what Queequeg tries, we cannot repair her. My crew, those "resurrected" sailors, have long since forgotten how to wield their harpoons. They no longer know how to fight the sea.
 
And it seems as though the whale is toying with me. Since that time, whether at sea or ashore, I have never laid eyes on it again. I do not wish to give up. I refuse to. As long as I can kill it, I will be freed from this curse-like "blessing" to find eternal rest.
 
But I... I am too old now. I can no longer lift a harpoon. I cannot fight that giant creature aboard one of these tiny "Gondolas."
 
Yes, my ideals, my beliefs, my fate, my vengeance—everything is gone. Everything has been swallowed by these foreign seas.
 
You are, of course, welcome to mock me. The rope of that harpoon, while I lived, bound me tightly to that whale. Even now, after death, I am still bound by it. In the past, I was unwilling to sever that rope. Now, I remain unwilling still...  But I can no longer drag it into the black depths of the sea.
 
Sometime later, a young man came to find me. He said his name was Ishmael, a sailor's apprentice, and he wanted to learn how to fish.
 
At that moment, I recalled that before Pequod's final voyage, there was a sailor named Ishmael at the Bedford dock. But he did not board my ship. He stayed at the port, and if he is still alive at sea, he would likely be as old as I am now. How ironic...

For people like us, the end of the world is the end of the sea.
 
I was born by the sea, died on the sea, and finally will be buried under the sea.
 
This time, I could not kill it. But next time I will certainly kill it... certainly.

The Golden Anthem Anthology

Literary works draw their vitality from two sources: The creator and the readers.

The creator gives it new life, while the readers help extend it through reading. Each time they share a piece of work or publish their thoughts and reviews, they breathe new life into it.

Some may find the term "life of a work" elusive, as it's too abstract and intangible.

However, a parallel can be easily drawn from human life. When discussing the concept of life, one essential topic is inevitably brought up—name. A name is a symbol of existence, one of the most important markers that separate individual lives. If one desires to feel the vitality of a work, the most direct approach would be to feel its name, the various names bestowed by creators and readers.

I once heard an eerie tale from a land in the east that spoke of a lady with skin as fair as snow who would stand in a snowstorm, cradling a wailing baby in her arms, begging the passersby to hold the baby for her. If some kindhearted individual agrees to that request, they'd soon find themselves unable to let go, bound to freeze to death.

Intriguing, isn't it? But, by this point, it's a fascinating tale that evokes many distinct images that cannot yet form the entirety of "life." 

But what if we give it a name? Like... "The Snow Woman." This name alone captures the entire narrative and defines its essence.

However, even with the name anchoring people's imaginations, the unusual nature of words means each person takes a narrative differently.

Hence... The life of a creative work is less controllable than human life.

So, if one day, people's understanding of a work is led astray, then words could turn into a devastating weapon.

What would we do then? Show anger? No, absolutely not! Anger is the cheapest outlet of dissent. As creators, all we can do is believe. Believe that our words can live in their most genuine form.
<alignright/>—Exclusive interview with the Golden Anthem

Preliminaries
The preliminaries follow a points-based system, with events including but not limited to: Echo Duels, Echo Speed Tests, and Echo Teamwork Challenges. These matches test a team's overall mastery of Echoes. At the end of the preliminaries, the top 20 teams by cumulative score will advance to the Finals.

Finals
The Finals follow a single-elimination format. The top 20 teams from the preliminaries, along with specially selected teams, will face off in one-on-one matches. Winners advance until the final match determines the Champion team.

Special Qualifiers
Also held in single-elimination format, the Special Qualifiers pit participants against each other in matches involving Echo vs. Echo or Echo vs. Gladiator combat. Victors inherit the defeated side's accumulated points. Once a participant reaches the required point threshold, they earn a direct entry into the Finals.

May 10th - This was our first mission with the advance squad, and I naively thought the Wuthering Waves weather was just normal. But it was far worse than I could have imagined.

May 11th - We were sent to Norfall Barrens to investigate Threnodian Crownless energy, but the Wuthering Waves only made things more difficult. The constant rain blurred our vision and we could barely see where we were going. General Jiyan gave us a potion to block out the strange whispers we heard in the weather.

May 13th - Our team was starting to feel overwhelmed as members fell one by one. For the first time, the idea of retreating crossed my mind. Thankfully General Jiyan recognized our distress and allowed us to rest in some ruins for the night. We found a book of jokes that helped ease our tensions, but General Jiyan still seemed worried.

May 20th - Wuthering Waves concentrations were no longer important because all data was meaningless. We were suffocating in this environment, and in our latest battle, everyone died except for me and General Jiyan. He sacrificed himself to save me from the TD army. I couldn't do anything but watch as he fought alone, his star mark flickering from overuse of his Resonator powers. I begged for help while hiding behind him, not wanting to die. In the end, General Jiyan half-knelt in the ruins while his lance stood tall, saving my life.

Tucked away in the tempestuous Stormy Sea lies an archipelago known for its lavish Tacetite deposits and as a refuge for the world's most talented individuals. With a mission to combat the destructive Lament, the Black Shores has fostered strong partnerships with nations across Solaris-3.

The archipelago cannot be accessed from any known lands. Only those recognized by the Black Shores or who have received an invitation and guidance can navigate their way to this hidden place.

Members of the Black Shores who operate abroad, frequently traversing various lands, are known as "Consultants." Those stationed at the headquarters are referred to as "Bloom Bearers." Apart from these fundamental duties, the Black Shores also accommodates a plethora of other specialized roles.

Though the Black Shores openly shares its advanced technologies with its partners, even its own members remain unaware of the true origins of these innovations.
The Black Shores

Also known as the Civilization Simulation Sand Table, the Tethys System is a supercomputer unique to the Black Shores. By inputting Lament frequency data—collected both manually and via beacon access—into the system, the Black Shores can issue Lament warnings for locations worldwide within a 24 to 48-hour time range. This capability is the cornerstone of the Black Shores' extensive collaborations with countries across the globe.

The results generated by the Tethys System are projected as a starry sky within the underground of the Black Shores, made possible by multiple Anchors and underground Data Hubs. This has earned the underground region the title "City of Eternal Night".

The Tethys System has no discernible energy source, physical infrastructure, or processing core. Its coding language is extremely complex, and it is only known that its terminals take the form of various autonomous robots. In essence, the Tethys System is almost akin to a natural phenomenon, with an origin that remains entirely mysterious.
The Tethys System

These unique robots, found throughout the Black Shores, serve as the physical terminals of the Tethys System. Their construction and performance capabilities remain largely unknown, yet they possess direct access to the system, second only to its administrator. Within the Black Shores, these robots function both as assistants and tools in the daily activities of its members.\n\nEach terminal has a distinct personality, and the study of these robots has advanced the field of cognitive psychology.
The Black Shores Robots

Based on the computational protocols of the Tethys System, the Stellar Matrix is a data package format that functions similarly to a highly compressed file. It has the capacity to store immense amounts of information and even simulate a Lament. Certain individuals can access these matrices under specific circumstances, making them an integral part of the Tethys System's operational framework.

Properly functioning Stellar Matrices are projected into the subterranean galaxy of the Black Shores, allowing members to study and observe them. Malfunctioning matrices, however, are collected and isolated in designated areas to prevent data overflow.
The first member to define a Stellar Matrix noted that standards of observing and evaluating one are similar to the astronomical standards of Solaris-3.
Stellar Matrix

Modulation is the process of adjusting frequencies. In Solaris-3, frequencies serve as a crucial tool for uncovering the truth about reality. By altering these frequencies, one can delve into the very core of existence.\n\nAt the Black Shores, modulating Stellar Matrices is crucial for tracing and analyzing the Lament. Over the course of the Black Shores' history, only one individual has ever been honored with the title of "The Modulator."
Modulation

A mysterious lifeform that rests beneath the Black Shores' subterranean galaxy. Her physical structure and age are shrouded in mystery. In the complicated coding language of the Tethys System, the name "Shorekeeper" also means "Guardian of Secrets". She chose to call herself "Shorekeeper" to symbolize her role in watching over those who venture away from the shores into faraway lands.
The Shorekeeper

These stabilizing devices are strategically positioned throughout the surface and underground parts of the Black Shores. Their primary function is to calibrate and stabilize the frequencies of the giant Tacetites that make up the island, effectively isolating the Tethys System's virtual layer from reality. Additionally, these Anchors facilitate communication and carry the responsibility of observing the Etheric Sea, eliminating the need to build a Nexus Tower in the Black Shores.\n\nThe Anchors are independently developed and designed by the Black Shores, drawing inspiration from the reactor control rods used in pre-Lament reactor engineering. They are considered exemplary models of the Black Shores' minimalist engineering design.
Anchor

A nation of independent city-states scattered across a vast archipelago, with no central administrative center. Legends speak of Rinascita's founders, who fled their homeland and sailed to these islands to escape the Lament. 

As an island nation reborn from the Lament, Rinascita was long isolated from the rest of the world by relentless disasters and vast distances. It wasn't until recent times that the Rinascitans opened new maritime routes. Ships laden with their spices and minerals began to sail across the world, and in turn, new treasures and wealth began flowing back to Rinascita, enriching its shores.

Rinascita is famed for its unique "Common Echo" technology, which allows Echoes to persist in physical form within the radius of the Genesis Nexus. Through this technology, the Rinascitan people have integrated Echoes into every facet of their lives. This is how the nation came to be known as the "Land of Echoes."

Rinascitans place great value on the identity derived from bloodlines, and their society is built upon a deep reverence for family ties. For them, the welfare of the family always takes precedence over individual fate.
Rinascita

Ragunna City, the administrative center of the Ragunna city-state in Rinascita, is a thriving port city by the sea, its districts linked by winding waterways. The Ragunnesi are devout followers of the Sentinel, who believe Common Echoes to be gifts from the Sentinel carrying Their divine will.

In addition to their faith, the people of Ragunna are also known for their love of the arts. The city is adorned with magnificent sculptures and paintings at every turn, and impromptu performances often bring the streets to life. Under the leadership of Fenrico, the current Primus of the Order of the Deep, a series of laws have been enacted to restrict certain themes in artistic expression. These laws have sparked divided opinion among the city's inhabitants.

At present, Ragunna's daily affairs are overseen by the Order of the Deep, while prominent families such as Montelli and Fisalia also hold significant influence over the direction of the city.
Ragunna City

The Carnevale is the grandest celebration of Ragunna, where the masquerades never end, wine flows like rivers, and music pulses through the night. During this time, people cast aside the weight of the world and surrender to the wild, unrestrained joy of the festival.

The Carnevale's origins trace back to Sentinel Imperator, who once guided the people of Rinascita. It began as a tribute to Their grace, a celebration where laughter and performance became the purest form of reverence.

At the peak of the Carnevale, the Sentinel is said to manifest and crown the finest performer with the "Laurel." This honor grants the bearer the privilege to commune with the Sentinel and hear Their wisdom.

Yet, a decade ago, the Carnevale was brought to ruin. A monstrous sea beast, rogue Echoes, and Tacet Discords swept through the festival, turning revelry to ruin. Only when Primus Fenrico intervened did the chaos subside. He proclaimed it was Sentinel Imperator's divine retribution for the Ragunnesi's indulgence and forsaking of their faith. Since then, the Carnevale has not been held again.
Carnevale

Those deemed faithless by the Order of the Deep are sent to voyage upon the Pilgrim's Sail, following the ancient path of those who once braved the mist and maelstrom seeking the Sentinel's guidance.

The Order claims that only Imperator can grant absolution to these transgressors. They must endure a grueling pilgrimage, suffering both body and soul until their repentance is complete. At the journey's end, it is said Sentinel Imperator will offer them forgiveness and the promise of new life.

But no one in Ragunna has ever heard of a faithless "pilgrim" returning from this sacred journey. The Order asserts that they reach Imperator's place of dwelling and devote themselves to Their service for eternity. While many still harbor doubts, few dare to openly challenge the Order—none wish to suffer the same tragic fate as those branded Fools.
Pilgrim's Sail

A common boat-shaped Echo in Ragunna.

Ragunna's intricate network of waterways, coupled with its narrow streets and rugged terrain surrounding the city has made Gondolas the preferred choice for transporting both people and goods. For most Ragunnesi, they offer a peaceful, smooth alternative to the discomfort of navigating crowded streets or bumpy countryside roads.

Beneath their unassuming exterior, Gondolas are highly intelligent and deeply emotional. They communicate through distinct vocal frequencies, expressing their moods or responding to the command of their gondolier. Some, through specialized training, can even climb waterfalls.
Gondola

The Order of the Deep worships Sentinel Imperator. In Ragunna tradition, the Order's clergy serve as the Sentinel's earthly envoys, entrusted with guiding the people in Their divine word.

The Order is led by the Primus, and the current Primus, Fenrico, has declared himself the "Enlightened One," the Resonator of the Sentinel. After the last Carnevale, he proclaimed to have discovered the way to commune directly with the Sentinel.

Beneath the Primus, the Priests oversee the rites and sacred duties of the Order, while the common clergy, known as Acolytes, spend their days poring over the Codex, spreading the Sentinel's teachings throughout Ragunna.

To uphold divine order, the Order commands three distinct branches:

Order Tribunal: The Order's secular judicial body that handles civil and criminal matters between families and commoners.

Chamber of Discipline: The Order's executive arm that commands the military to enforce the law. The Chamber heavily employs Echoes in combat, and its enforcers are often called "Inquisitors."

Order Penitentiary: The Order's religious court that trials heretics and faithless who question and defy the divine teachings of the Sentinel.
Order of the Deep

One of the most powerful families in Ragunna, renowned for their pioneering spirit. The Montelli family played an instrumental role in charting trade routes that not only connect Ragunna, but also greater Rinascita to the wider world. As the city opened its doors, the Montellis rose to prominence, amassing great wealth and unmatched influence.

The Montelli family also took the lead in introducing and developing Reserved Terminals across Ragunna. While the Order of the Deep dismissed these Terminals as an inferior mockery of the Genesis Nexus and Common Echoes, the Montellis secured the Order's approval to continue their development in secrecy, offering guarantees of safety and hefty tax payment in exchange.

Unlike the more traditional families, the Montelli family values emotional bonds and shared ideals above bloodlines and social standing. They advocate for the distribution of opportunities and wealth, believing that riches are worth more when they circulate. Though often ridiculed by traditional families as "nouveau riche with Shell Credits running through their veins," the Montellis take no offense—on the contrary, they wear the label with pride.
Montelli

One of the most powerful, and certainly the oldest and most traditional, families in Ragunna, renowned for their expertise in medicine and poison. Their devotion to Sentinel Imperator is clear to all who know them.\n\nA faction within the Fisalia family believes that the Montelli family's embrace of openness and the privatization of Echoes is a direct affront to Imperator's teachings, threatening to lead Ragunna into an abyss of heresy. They have directly opposed the Montellis through various means, shaking the family's longstanding image of dignified respectability. Yet, the head of the Fisalia family residing in Porto-Veno Castle seems disturbingly indifferent to the repercussions of these bold and provocative actions.
Fisalia

The Sentinel of Rinascita. In the faith of the Order of the Deep, They are often depicted as a being with the upper body of a horse and the lower body of a fish.

According to Ragunna's legends, Imperator guided its settlers to this promised land, offering them sanctuary from the threat of the Lament.

Though Imperator rarely reveals Their presence to the world, They maintain a connection with the people of Ragunna through the Laureate of the Carnevale, delivering divine guidance in the form of oracles.
Imperator

In Rinascita, most Echoes can exist independently from Reserved Terminals within the radius of the Genesis Nexus. They are known as Common Echoes.\n\nIn Ragunna, the Order of the Deep governs the allocation and use of these Echoes. The people of Ragunna revere them as divine gifts, even as envoys of Sentinel Imperator. They treat them as friends and trusted allies, incorporating them into every aspect of daily life. This deep, symbiotic bond with Common Echoes is what has earned Rinascita its name as the "Land of Echoes."
Common Echo

Rinascita's central Resonance Nexus, also known as the Genesis Nexus. According to legend, Imperator revealed the secrets of the Genesis Nexus to the Rinascitans, enabling them to construct other such towering monuments that stand as symbols of the Sentinel's power and sovereignty.\n\nWithin the reach of the Genesis Nexus, Echoes can endure in physical form without relying on Terminals.
Genesis Nexus

The Dark Tide is a Waveworn Phenomenon native to Rinascita. It manifests as a dark, swirling mass of clouds that gathers and eventually breaks, pouring down in torrents like a waterfall. Wherever the Dark Tide strikes, it spawns Tacet Discords, and the area around its point of origin becomes a new Tacet Field.\n\nThere have been two significant Dark Tides in Ragunna's history. The first, according to the Order of the Deep, was stopped by Napoli II, the first Primus of the Order. The second was quelled by the martyrdom of the Blessed Maiden Fleurdelys.
Dark Tide

The Nimbus Sanctum is the only Sonoro Sphere that exists in the physical world, where mist and clouds are formed by concentrated Remnant Energy.

The sea of clouds that envelop the Sanctum is believed to be the lingering aftermath of the first Dark Tide. As the mist rose, it gradually submerged the former headquarters of the Order of the Deep, the Seminary of the Forgotten, forcing them to relocate to the Cathedral of Mercury in Ragunna City.

Local legends of Ragunna speak of a serene, mirror-like area at the heart of Nimbus Sanctum, said to purify the darkest of thoughts and transform them into part of the clouds. Many pilgrims, drawn by this tale, journey here in search of inner peace.
Nimbus Sanctum

The Remnant Creature dwelling within Nimbus Sanctum. Legend holds that it was Lorelei's power that restrained the violent sea of clouds, sparing Ragunna from flooding.\n\nLorelei has the ability to cleanse the dark frequencies within the clouds, but she is not immune to their corrosive influence. As they accumulate to a breaking point, Lorelei will eventually become the Queen of the Night, unleashing her wrath upon all life that comes near.
Lorelei
